summary: Automate rotation of CI service-account tokens with graceful overlap to prevent job failures
description: Issue summary: Our central CI service account tokens (used by self-hosted GitHub/GitLab runners and several release pipelines) are rotated manually by SRE. This creates short windows where scheduled or push-triggered jobs observe auth errors. Impact: intermittent CI failures during releases, flaky deploys and developer friction. Goal: design and implement an automated rotation flow that provides an overlapping grace period (dual-valid tokens) and a rollback path in case a rotation causes failures.
impact: Multiple release pipelines across teams experience sporadic authentication errors (401/403) during manual token swaps. Recent incident increased mean time to merge for a hotfix by ~90 minutes and blocked one nightly build. Affects platform and product teams that rely on self-hosted runners and the release automation service account.
environment_details: Tokens are stored in Vault (transit+kv v2). Runners pull short-lived credentials via the internal token-proxy service. Current rotate procedure: generate new token in Vault, update token-proxy, and then revoke old token immediately. Runners poll token-proxy on restart or job start; some long-lived runner processes cache token until restart.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Coordinate with SRE to trigger manual token rotation in Vault (generate new secret, write to path used by token-proxy)
2) Deploy token-proxy configuration change to point to new secret version
3) Trigger a concurrent release pipeline run on a self-hosted runner that has a cached token
4) Observe the job failing with 401/403 while the runner is still using the old token after it has been revoked
observed_behavior: Jobs started by runners that still hold the old token fail with 401/403 until runners are recycled. Job logs show errors from token validation endpoint and 401 responses from the control-plane auth check.
expected_behavior: Rotation should not cause running or newly-scheduled jobs to fail. We should have a transition window where both the old and new tokens are accepted until all runners have picked up the new token, or runners are gracefully instructed to rotate without aborting in-progress jobs.
investigation_notes: Checked vault audit logs (vault-audit-2026-03-09): immediate revoke events at 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z correlated with first 401 spike
Token-proxy logs (token-proxy-prod-2026-03-09): config reload succeeded; no explicit dual-token handling present
Runner processes: several teams run long-lived runner containers that only refresh credentials on container restart — documented in runbooks but not consistently enforced
Hypothesis: immediate revokes combined with long-lived cached tokens cause timing windows where in-flight jobs see token invalidation
Quick test: applied a prototype dual-acceptance patch to token-proxy to accept previous token for 10 minutes — jobs that would have failed succeeded in test cluster
Related runbooks: Confluence - CI Token Rotation Runbook (https://confluence.internal/redwood/ci-token-rotation)
comments: Benicio Reyes (2026-03-10): Assigned to Priya for design. Initial approach: implement a rotator that writes new token version to Vault and updates token-proxy, leaving previous version accepted for a configurable grace_seconds parameter. Need orchestration that optionally sends graceful restart signal to runners that support hot-reload.

Priya Singh (2026-03-11): Ran a canary in staging using grace_seconds=600; token-proxy accepted both v1 and v2 for the window. Observed no failing jobs in staging. Two blockers: (1) some runner images don't support hot-reload and need restart orchestration; (2) Vault revocation API currently used by ops revokes immediately — need delayed-revoke or scheduled revoke.

SRE Oncall (Liam O'Connor) (2026-03-11): Proposed changes to ops process: change manual revoke to schedule revoke job that runs after grace window. Also suggested adding a health-check endpoint for token-proxy to report last rotation time.

Devops (Marina Velasquez) (2026-03-12): Noted one edge-case for private clusters (on-prem runners) where network lag causes longer token propagation — recommend 15 minute default grace in cross-region pools.

Priya Singh (2026-03-12): Working on a design doc and implementation plan. Will submit PR for token-proxy to support accepting previous token version and a CLI tool for scheduled revokes. Targeting rollout to prod-ci in two phases: token-proxy change + scheduled revoke orchestration (phase 1), runner restart orchestration (phase 2).
proposal_summary: Implement a three-part safe-rotation flow: (A) token-proxy supports dual-accept for previous secret version for a configurable grace_seconds; (B) rotation orchestration script that: creates new token secret, updates token-proxy, schedules a revoke job in Vault after grace_seconds; (C) review and gradually deploy runner hot-reload/restart automation for long-lived runners so that they pick up new tokens without manual restarts.
action_items: Design and land token-proxy PR to accept previous secret version (owner: Priya)
Add scheduled revoke utility to ops-tooling to revoke vault secrets after grace window (owner: SRE)
Inventory long-lived runner pools and add restart hooks where feasible (owner: DevOps)
Update CI runbooks and add 'recommended grace window' defaults per region (owner: Documentation)
Run phased rollout in staging, then prod-ci with 15 minute default grace for cross-region pools (owner: Release Engineering)
resolution: In Progress - prototype validated in staging; production rollout scheduled. Resolution pending completion of token-proxy PR and scheduled revoke tooling. Follow-ups: create monitoring alert for post-rotation 5xx/401 spike and add a post-rotation checklist in runbook.
final_notes: Avoid immediate revokes in manual process until tooling is in place. Prefer automated rotations that include observability and a rollback path. Planned next update: PR link and rollout schedule by 2026-03-15.
